figure: Figure 17.1 (Sizing a fleet of one model)
issue: Self-contradiction between the in-figure top-right annotation and the caption: both state the N-1 residual 'clears the burst only at ρ = 1' while simultaneously giving a break-even threshold of 'need ≥ 0.917' / 'ρ ≥ 0.917 is needed to clear it'. If 0.917 is the threshold, the residual also clears at ρ = 0.95, so 'only at ρ = 1' is literally false and overstates the fragility of the reserve (a skimmer could conclude the 4th host is useless unless efficiency is exactly 100%).
evidence: Top-right block: 'N-1 clears the burst only at ρ = 1: at ρ = 0.85 the residual = ~5.1 < ~5.5, need ≥ 0.917.' Caption caveat: 'the N−1 = 3 residual (~6.0 req/s) clears the burst only at ρ = 1 — at ρ = 0.85 it is 3 × 2.0 × 0.85 ≈ 5.1 req/s, below the ~5.5 burst (ρ ≥ 0.917 is needed to clear it)'. The arithmetic (5.5/6.0 = 0.9167) is correct; only the 'only at ρ = 1' phrasing contradicts it.
acceptance_test: Reword both the in-figure annotation and the caption so the stated condition is the break-even value, e.g. 'at the ideal ρ = 1 the N-1 residual (6.0) clears the 5.5 burst with 0.5 margin; the break-even is ρ ≈ 0.917, so any efficiency loss below that breaks failover'. Confirm no remaining clause asserts the residual works exclusively at ρ = 1.

issue: Color-semantic collision: the start node 'Request' uses the same blue fill as the specialist-family leaves (Embedding, Vision, Math/reason). Blue therefore encodes two different roles (a process/start node vs. a model-family category), so a reader could misread 'Request' as a specialist model. The decision nodes are orange and the non-specialist leaves are teal/green, which is consistent; only the Request/specialist blue overlap is muddled.
evidence: Visual: 'Request' box fill matches the 'Embedding'/'Vision'/'Math/reason' box fill; the in-figure note 'policy: capability first, then cost/SLO, then general fallback' does not re-key the colors.
acceptance_test: Give 'Request' a distinct neutral fill (e.g., mid-gray) so blue unambiguously denotes the specialist family; add or adjust the fill key to state the convention. Confirm the tree still reads left-to-right with no new ambiguity.

figure: Figure 19.1 (The agent loop: a four-state machine)
issue: Low-contrast italic sub-annotations: the role labels inside the state boxes ('model', 'action', 'state', 'check', 'read, plan', 'tool call', 'append result', 'resolved?', 'emit', 'done', 'limit', 'terminal') are rendered in light gray italic on pale-blue (top row) and amber (bottom row) fills. In color the contrast is marginal; in grayscale the pale-blue boxes become near-white and the light-gray text (notably 'resolved?', the actual decision predicate in the Decide state) becomes hard to read, degrading the figure's grayscale interpretability.
evidence: Visual: compare the bold dark main labels (Plan/Execute/Observe/Decide/Final answer/Stopped) with the faint italic sub-labels; 'resolved?' and 'check' in the Decide box are the lightest text on the lightest fill.
acceptance_test: Darken all sub-annotation text to a dark gray/black (or remove the pale-blue fill behind them) so every sub-label, including 'resolved?', is legible when the page is converted to grayscale; re-render and verify no sub-label falls below comfortable contrast on either the blue or amber fills.
